MarketScreener insider profile page for Scott Stowell, not a news story

articles.summary: PulteGroup reported lower third-quarter 2026 earnings, with fewer closings and falling new orders as higher mortgage rates hurt affordability.
articles.why_it_matters: Syndicated recap of PulteGroup's Q3 miss; adds nothing beyond the kept item on Pulte's possible 2027 land-spend cut.

articles.summary: KB Home's Orlando division closed Sept. 28 on a 40-acre Apopka, Florida tract for $7.1 million, planned for more than 100 homes.
articles.why_it_matters: A small direct raw-land purchase by KB Home in Orlando shows it is still buying land itself in Central Florida, a market where Domain could offer to finance the lots instead.

articles.summary: Toll Brothers bought a 47.92-acre parcel at 1336 Limekiln Pike in Ambler, Pennsylvania, for 34 luxury single-family homes, per a Philadelphia Business Journal report.
articles.why_it_matters: A small, single-community land buy by Toll in suburban Philadelphia; too small to change Toll's need for land-bank capital.

articles.summary: About 100 West Brandywine Township residents attended a hearing opposing Toll Brothers' proposed 237-home age-restricted community.
articles.why_it_matters: Same local entitlement fight as the kept MyChesCo item; entitlement risk on one Toll community, nothing for Domain to act on.

articles.summary: HousingWire analysis of D.R. Horton's fiscal 2027 planning after its Sept. 30 year-end, suggesting a likely closings range of 82,000 to 86,000 homes and continued pricing and incentive discipline.
articles.why_it_matters: The closings range is a trade-press estimate, not company guidance; Horton's actual volume plan, now published, is the better read on how many lots it will need.

articles.summary: PulteGroup's Q3 2026 revenue fell 9.8% to $3.97 billion and adjusted EPS was $2.53, both below estimates; backlog rose 3.4% to $6.44 billion and management said it may reduce land spend in 2027.
articles.why_it_matters: If the third-largest builder cuts 2027 land spend, it will need fewer new optioned lots, which shrinks one source of demand for land-bank capital.

articles.summary: WSJ: PulteGroup's third-quarter net income and revenue fell sharply as high mortgage rates slowed sales and weighed on prices.
articles.why_it_matters: Paywalled copy of PulteGroup's Q3 miss; the kept item carries the land-spend comment that matters to Domain.

articles.summary: NVR reported Q3 2026 net income of $248.6 million, or $89.45 per diluted share; net income fell 27% and EPS 20% from a year earlier.
articles.why_it_matters: NVR controls its lots through option contracts rather than owning land, so a sharp profit drop there shows the pressure on builders that rely on optioned lots.

articles.summary: Bloomberg: PulteGroup and NVR both missed quarterly earnings estimates as high mortgage rates and global turmoil hurt sales.
articles.why_it_matters: Paywalled roundup of the same Pulte and NVR misses scored elsewhere in this batch; no new facts for Domain.

articles.summary: Yahoo Finance valuation piece arguing Sekisui House shares (TSE:1928, ¥3,431) may be slightly undervalued on cash flow after a 79.5% five-year gain.
articles.why_it_matters: A stock-valuation note on the Japanese parent; nothing about Sekisui House U.S. land or financing needs.

articles.drop: Different subject: Devon Horton, a former school superintendent, not D.R. Horton

articles.summary: Toll Brothers faces heavy public opposition to a proposed 237-home age-restricted community on about 116 acres near Hibernia County Park in West Brandywine Township, Pennsylvania.
articles.why_it_matters: Entitlement risk on one Toll community in Chester County; a local fight with no capital decision for Domain.

articles.summary: Thor Equities is proposing a roughly $1 billion data center on a wooded site just north of Cartersville, Georgia, per Bisnow's Atlanta deal sheet.
articles.why_it_matters: A data-center land deal with no homebuilder or land-bank angle; at most a sign of competing demand for land in exurban Atlanta.

articles.summary: As of Nov. 4, holders had tendered $248.1M of $250M Beazer 7.500% notes due 2031 and $393.1M of $400M 8.000% notes due 2032 into Dream Finders' exchange offer for new Dream Finders notes. The covenant-stripping consents passed; the offer expires Nov. 20 and settles about Nov. 23.
articles.why_it_matters: Dream Finders is taking on about $640M of Beazer's notes as its own debt after the Beazer acquisition, which shows how much the combined company has borrowed and how much capacity it has for land-light financing of Beazer's lot pipeline.

suggested_update.text: Nov. 2026: about 99% of Beazer's $250M 7.500% 2031 and 98% of its $400M 8.000% 2032 notes tendered for new Dream Finders notes; covenants stripped, settlement expected Nov. 23, 2026.

articles.summary: Tri Pointe Homes reported third-quarter and nine-month results to Sept. 30, 2026, with Q3 revenue of $707.58 million (French-language MarketScreener wire).
articles.why_it_matters: A bare results wire with no lot, land-spend or leverage detail; Tri Pointe's own release is the better source for its land needs.

articles.summary: LGI Homes closed 297 homes in October 2026, including 9 current or former single-family rentals, and had 151 active communities at Oct. 31.
articles.why_it_matters: A routine monthly closings update; it only confirms the 151-community base behind LGI's growth target.

articles.summary: On its Q3 call, LGI said it amended its revolver (about $1.17B of commitments, $855M now due Oct. 2030), targets more than 180 communities by end-2027 from 151, partly on finished lots bought from developers, and narrowed 2026 closings to 4,600 to 4,800.
articles.why_it_matters: LGI, which mostly owns its land, plans 20% community growth and will buy more finished lots from developers, so it may want lot-option financing; its extended revolver is the bank capital Domain would compete with.

suggested_update.text: Oct. 9, 2026: revolver amended to about $1.166B of commitments ($855M extended to Oct. 2030) plus a $175M incremental facility; Q3 liquidity was $447.7M.

articles.summary: Fitch said insured losses from Hurricane Isaias, expected in the mid-single-digit billions, are unlikely to affect the ratings of major US property and casualty reinsurers.
articles.why_it_matters: A reinsurance rating note with no homebuilder, land or builder-financing angle; noise for Domain.
